title: Frontier Probe Orchestrator: kernel-aware routing, staged acceptance, and deterministic fallback playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: implement a lightweight runtime orchestration layer (Frontier Probe Orchestrator) that selects kernel+model candidate lanes for speculative decode, emits an early acceptance signal based on multi-stage heuristics, and falls back deterministically to a safe path when acceptance confidence is low. This ticket focuses on the runtime wiring, acceptance metrics, and an operational fallback playbook; it intentionally avoids model training or large-scale hyperparameter tuning (those belong to Applied ML).

Motivation: speculative decode can reduce average latency by attempting a fast, permissive decoding lane and accepting its output early when confidence is high. In practice we've observed edge cases where optimistic acceptance silently degrades quality or consumes expensive kernels without clear rollback behavior. The orchestrator must be kernel-aware (avoid scheduling heavy kernels for probes unless acceptance justifies it), provide measurable acceptance metrics (TPR/FPR on acceptance heuristics), and guarantee deterministic fallback to a slower but quality-safe decoder when needed.

Scope and constraints:
- Runtime-only changes: scheduler, router, acceptance evaluator, and fallback controller.
- Must integrate with kernel selection subsystem (kernel fingerprints, capacity signals).
- Must emit structured telemetry for per-request acceptance decisioning and allow offline evaluation.
- Rollouts must support canary percent, metric thresholds, and automatic rollback.
- Latency SLOs: optimistic fast-lane target p50 < 30ms extra overhead; fallback path must respect existing 99p latency SLOs.
- No changes to model weights or tokenization in this ticket.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator can register candidate lanes (fast, baseline, safe) with kernel affinity metadata
Acceptance evaluator emits an acceptance_score [0..1] and a binary accept/reject per request
If acceptance is false, request is routed to deterministic fallback lane with a guaranteed quality model variant
Telemetry: per-lane counts, accepted_rate, acceptance_precision, acceptance_recall, and cost delta are exported to the metrics pipeline
Unit + integration tests for routing decisions with mocked kernel capacity and synthetic confidence distributions
Canary rollout configuration exists in console with automated rollback when acceptance_recall drops >5% relative to baseline during window
notes: Design doc: Confluence -> /colours/runtime/frontier-probe-orchestrator (internal). See diagram: lane registration, kernel fingerprints, acceptance evaluator, fallback controller
Kernel affinity: use existing kernel signature API (runtime/kernel/signature) to tag lanes. Avoid scheduling probe lane on kernels with >70% load.

Acceptance heuristics considered: log-prob delta between lanes, token-level alignment score, early termination token patterns, and model-agnostic confidence head. We'll start with a lightweight log-prob delta + length-normalized prefix agreement metric.

Telemetry knobs: emit request_id, lane_chosen, acceptance_score, accept_decision, fallback_taken, kernel_fingerprint, decode_time_ms, tokens_generated_count, and cost_estimate_usd as tags/fields in metrics.
Fallback safety: fallback lane is pinned to a verified model variant (from model-catalog) and uses conservative kernel selection (high-accuracy kernels even if slightly slower).
